exercises.title: Inventory the existing environment

exercises.purpose: Which parts of the laptop can this WSL shell actually see?
exercises.before: Start in the prepared WSL2 working directory.

: "${LAB_RUN:?Run source reader/new_run.sh first}"
bash inventory.sh --out "$LAB_RUN/inventory.txt"
exercises.inspect: Open $LAB_RUN/inventory.txt. Read each command and its exit. If nvidia-smi was unavailable, the report identifies both skipped GPU queries.
exercises.interpret: A management query and a visible device interface are inventory evidence. Exercise 14 separately tests CUDA computation.
exercises.troubleshoot: If nvidia-smi is missing from PATH, inspect /usr/lib/wsl/lib. Retain a failed query; do not infer a missing Linux display driver.

exercises.handoff: Use the architecture and free disk space for Exercise 4. Keep the inventory path for the snapshot in Exercise 20.
exercises.evidence_note:

exercises.inspect: Read the context=4096 line in $LAB_RUN/budget/stdout.txt and check the exit in metadata.json.
exercises.interpret: An estimate is a planning input. Runtime buffers, context, concurrent sequences and host pressure still require measurement.
exercises.troubleshoot: If your estimate differs from the example, check whether you used KV heads or query heads and whether you counted both keys and values.
exercises.finish: Keep the estimate and its assumptions beside the later measured placement.
exercises.handoff: Carry the 4096-token prediction from budget/stdout.txt to the startup log in Exercise 5.

exercises.origin: NEW READER PROCEDURE; not a newly executed laptop transcript
exercises.check: Reproduce the byte estimate from context length, layer count, KV heads and element width. Save the 4096-token prediction for Exercise 5.
